name: Geography trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about countries, capitals, rivers, mountains, landmarks, maps. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: What does it mean to call Kilimanjaro a "free-standing" mountain?
answers: It is not part of a mountain range
It has never been covered by snow
It rises directly out of the sea
items.correct: It is not part of a mountain range
items.explain: Kilimanjaro is described as the world's largest free-standing mountain rise, meaning it does not belong to a mountain range. It is a stratovolcano.

items.question: Kilimanjaro is made up of three volcanic cones. Two are Kibo and Mawenzi. What is the third?
items.explain: The three cones of Kilimanjaro are Kibo, Mawenzi and Shira. Kibo is the tallest and holds the summit.

items.question: The highest point on Kilimanjaro's Kibo crater rim is called Uhuru. What does "uhuru" mean in Swahili?
items.explain: Uhuru is the Swahili word for freedom. The summit was renamed Uhuru Peak after independence.

items.question: Which lake, at roughly 1,642 metres deep, is the deepest in the world?
items.explain: Lake Baikal in southern Siberia reaches a maximum depth of about 1,642 metres (5,387 feet). Lake Tanganyika is second deepest.

source.title: Deepest Lake in the World - Deepest Lake in the United States

items.question: Lake Baikal is extremely deep because it sits in what kind of geological setting?
items.explain: Baikal lies in an active continental rift that is slowly widening and deepening through subsidence.

source.title: Deepest Lake in the World - Deepest Lake in the United States

items.question: Which Siberian city lies close to Lake Baikal?
items.explain: Lake Baikal is in southern Siberia, near the city of Irkutsk.

items.question: Which river is the main outflow of Lake Baikal?
items.explain: Many rivers feed Baikal, but its primary outflow is the Angara River.

items.question: Through how many countries does the Danube River pass, according to Britannica?
items.explain: The Danube passes through ten countries, from Germany to Ukraine.

items.question: The Danube is the second-longest river in Europe. Which river is the longest?
items.explain: The Volga in Russia is the longest river in Europe, and the Danube comes second.

items.question: Which of these capital cities does the Danube flow through?
items.explain: The Danube flows through four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade. Prague, Warsaw and Zagreb lie on other rivers.

items.question: In which German upland region does the Danube have its source?
items.explain: The Danube begins at Donaueschingen in Germany's Black Forest, where the Brigach and Breg streams meet.

items.question: Which two bodies of water does the Strait of Gibraltar connect?
answers: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Atlantic Ocean and the Baltic Sea
The Black Sea and the Aegean Sea
The Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea
items.correct: The Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea
items.explain: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow passage linking the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea. It also separates Europe from Africa.

items.question: Across the Strait of Gibraltar from southern Spain lies the northern coast of which African country?
items.explain: The strait separates Spain and Gibraltar to the north from Morocco, including Ceuta, to the south.

items.question: At its narrowest point, roughly how wide is the Strait of Gibraltar?
items.explain: The narrowest distance between the Rock of Gibraltar and Morocco is about 14 km (7.7 nautical miles).

source.title: Strait of Gibraltar - Simple English Wikipedia

items.question: The Atacama Desert, the driest non-polar desert on Earth, lies mainly in which country?
items.explain: The Atacama stretches along the Pacific coast of northern Chile, between the Andes and the coastal range.

source.title: What's So Special About the Atacama Desert? - Live Science

items.question: On average, how much rain does the driest part of the Atacama Desert receive each year?
items.explain: The driest part of the Atacama gets under a millimetre of rain a year on average, which is why it is so extreme.

source.title: What's So Special About the Atacama Desert? - Live Science

items.question: Scientists study the Atacama Desert's soils partly because they resemble those found on which planet?
items.explain: Comparisons with data from Mars rovers showed that Atacama soils have many similarities to Martian soils.

source.title: The driest place on earth - UC Berkeley

items.question: Which city is Bolivia's constitutional capital, home to its Supreme Court?
items.explain: Sucre is the constitutional capital and seat of the judiciary. La Paz is the administrative capital.

items.question: Bolivia is landlocked. Which of these countries does NOT border it?
items.explain: Bolivia borders Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Chile and Peru. Ecuador does not share a border with it.

items.question: Bolivia was named in honour of which South American liberator?
items.explain: Bolivia's 1825 congress named the new country after Simón Bolívar. Antonio José de Sucre led the army that liberated Upper Peru and gave his name to the capital city.

items.question: Which of these national capitals sits highest above sea level?
items.explain: La Paz, Bolivia's seat of government, lies at more than 3,000 metres and is described as the highest national capital in the world.

items.question: Which city did Brasília replace as Brazil's capital?
items.explain: Brasília was planned to move the capital from coastal Rio de Janeiro to a more central location.

items.question: In which year was Brasília founded as Brazil's new national capital?
items.explain: President Juscelino Kubitschek founded Brasília on 21 April 1960.

items.question: Which modernist architect worked with planner Lúcio Costa on the design of Brasília?
items.explain: Brasília was planned by Lúcio Costa, and the architect Niemeyer designed many of its landmark buildings.

items.question: Victoria Falls is formed by which river?
items.explain: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River, about midway along its course.

items.question: Victoria Falls lies on the border between which two countries?
items.explain: The falls sit on the Zambezi, with Zambia to the north and Zimbabwe to the south.

items.question: Victoria Falls is known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya. What does that name mean?
items.explain: Mosi-oa-Tunya translates as "The Smoke That Thunders", after the mist and roar of the falls.

items.question: In which country is Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall?
items.explain: Angel Falls is in Canaima National Park in Bolívar State, Venezuela. It drops about 979 metres in total.

items.question: Angel Falls was named after which aviator?
items.explain: The falls are named after the aviator Jimmy Angel, who brought them to wider attention in the 1930s.

items.question: Angel Falls plunges from the top of which table-top mountain?
items.explain: The falls drop from Auyán-tepui in Canaima National Park.

items.question: Which ancient people made Petra the capital of their kingdom?
items.explain: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom, which grew rich from controlling trade routes such as the Incense Road.

source.title: The Ancient City of Petra - American Museum of Natural History

items.question: Visitors reach Petra's Treasury through a winding gorge. What is it called?
items.explain: Visitors walk through the Siq, a winding gorge, and first see Al Khazna (the Treasury) carved in rosy sandstone.

source.title: Petra, Jordan, archaeology and history - National Geographic

items.question: In 1812, which adventurer, disguised as a Muslim pilgrim, reached Petra and revealed it to the Western world?
items.explain: The Swiss explorer Johann Burckhardt posed as a pilgrim to persuade a Bedouin guide to take him to Petra. Many Westerners had thought the city a myth.

source.title: Petra, Jordan, archaeology and history - National Geographic

items.question: The name Petra comes from the Greek word for what?
items.explain: Petra is the Greek name for the Nabataean capital Raqmu, and the word means "rock".

source.title: Kingdom of Nabatea - World History Encyclopedia

items.question: The Ural Mountains form the traditional boundary between which two continents?
items.explain: The Urals run through west-central Russia and form the main part of the traditional Europe–Asia boundary.

items.question: What is the highest peak of the Ural Mountains?
items.explain: Mount Narodnaya, at about 1,895 metres, is the highest peak in the Urals.

items.question: The Ural River, conventionally part of the Europe–Asia boundary, empties into which body of water?
items.explain: The Ural is one of the major rivers, with the Volga and Terek, that empty into the northern Caspian Sea.

items.question: In which year did the Panama Canal open to shipping?
items.explain: The canal opened on 15 August 1914, after the United States completed the work.

items.question: Which country's company began building the Panama Canal in 1881, before the project collapsed in 1889?
items.explain: A French company started the canal in 1881 but failed. The United States took over in 1904.

items.question: In which year did Panama take full control of the Panama Canal?
items.explain: A 1977 treaty provided for handover by 2000, and Panama took control in 1999.

items.question: Ships crossing the Panama Canal pass through which large lake after the Gatún Locks?
items.explain: The canal runs from Colón through the Gatún Locks to Gatún Lake. It then continues toward the Bay of Panama.

items.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
items.explain: Lesotho is a landlocked enclave entirely encircled by South Africa. Eswatini also borders Mozambique.

items.question: What is the capital of Lesotho?
items.explain: Maseru is the capital and largest city of Lesotho.

items.question: Under a 1986 treaty, Lesotho built a large scheme to export which resource to South Africa?
items.explain: The Lesotho Highlands Water Treaty set up a transfer scheme exporting water to South Africa and producing hydroelectric power for Lesotho.

items.question: Which country is the smallest in the world by area, at about 0.44 square kilometres?
items.explain: Vatican City covers only about 0.17 square miles (0.44 sq km).

source.title: List of the smallest countries by area - Britannica

items.question: Which country ranks second in the world's smallest countries by area, behind Vatican City?
items.explain: Monaco, at about 0.8 square miles (2.1 sq km), comes closest behind Vatican City.

source.title: List of the smallest countries by area - Britannica

items.question: In which year did the Lateran Treaty recognise the sovereignty of Vatican City?
items.explain: The Italian government recognised Vatican City's sovereignty under the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929.

items.question: Which body of water is the world's largest inland body of water?
items.explain: The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water by surface area, and it is a salt lake.

items.question: Which of these countries has a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
items.explain: The Caspian borders five countries: Iran, Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan.

source.title: Caspian Sea: Largest Inland Water Body - Live Science

items.question: Which statement about the Caspian Sea's water is correct?
answers: It is fresh and drains to the Black Sea
It is salty and drains to the Persian Gulf
It is fresh and drains to the Arctic Ocean
It is salty and has no outlet to the ocean
items.correct: It is salty and has no outlet to the ocean
items.explain: The Caspian has no outlet and loses water only by evaporation, which lets salt accumulate. It is therefore not a freshwater lake.

source.title: Caspian Sea: Largest Inland Water Body - Live Science
